**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Regenerate the manifest with the current provider fingerprint**

The committed provider fingerprint does not match `make_config()` for the checked-in `future_family_delta`: I reproduced `2a698c0d...` under Python 3.12 and `3899734a...` under the repository's Python 3.11 CI version, rather than `7f736013...`. Consequently, `issue_1773_p4_kinematics_semantic_kg.py --check` always reports active-manifest drift, and the new test suite fails in `setUpClass`; regenerate the materialized manifest after the provider's final implementation is in place.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Compare the rebuilt P4-01 delta in successor mode**

When any successor shard is active, this branch verifies only the committed files against hard-coded receipts and never compares `build.bytes_by_path[DELTA]` with the historical delta. Thus a schema-valid change to the P4-01 provider or its configuration can make the deterministic rebuild produce different records while `--check` still prints `"deterministic_rebuild": "PASS"`; skip the shared projection and manifest, but retain an exact rebuilt-versus-committed comparison for the P4-01 delta.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

body: Fixed in 0332456c8. Successor mode now compares the rebuilt `build.bytes_by_path[DELTA]` byte-for-byte with the committed historical P4-01 delta while continuing to skip only the shared projection and manifest. A direct regression test covers this successor-manifest replay; the frozen P4-01 delta receipt remains 94a62888c2fc6ac8da788b233a9fe730e6424b08769a1d7c30eef476e3dc8148.

Fixed in 0332456c8. I regenerated the reviewed source, P4-02 delta, cumulative projection, and active manifest only after the final provider edits. The manifest now carries the current provider fingerprint, and `python3 scripts/vlm/issue_1773_p4_kinematics_semantic_kg.py --check` passes with physical corpus authentication and deterministic rebuild both PASS.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Regenerate the manifest with the current provider binding**

When this release is rebuilt or validated, `build_future_release(make_config())` computes `family_delta_provider_sha256` as `2a698c0d51ac8357ef4aaa9bdd4b639fcfdce56436982918072f0046d3db324b`, not the committed value. I reproduced this from a detached checkout of `d421907c` by running `python scripts/vlm/__tests__/issue_1773_p4_kinematics_semantic_kg.test.py`; `--check` fails with `materialized output drift: .../active-p4-release-manifest.json`, so the committed release cannot pass its deterministic custody check.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Regenerated at exact head 2154235bd after the final semantic-provider edit. `python3 scripts/vlm/issue_1773_p4_kinematics_semantic_kg.py --check` now passes with deterministic rebuild and physical corpus authentication both PASS, and the complete 74-test direct suite passes. The active manifest is materialized from the final source admission (source SHA-256 b3a502d2efc1c1ad93c3dcc3162984de250886775de931a79b81d5fd66053dba, length 48521).

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Regenerate the manifest with the admitted provider binding**

The committed provider binding does not match `make_config()` for this exact source, so `python3 scripts/vlm/issue_1773_p4_kinematics_semantic_kg.py --check` fails with `materialized output drift` and prevents the new test suite from reaching any tests. I reproduced this under Python 3.12, where the rebuild produces `2a698c0d...` rather than the committed `7f736013...`; Python 3.11 (used by repository workflows) produces `3899734a...`, so the artifact also cannot pass there. Regenerate this receipt for the intended runtime or make the provider fingerprint version-independent before committing the manifest.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve definitions for reused procedure-model IDs**

When a P4-02 instance reuses a P4-01 model ID, this unconditional assignment replaces the predecessor's canonical definition even though the copied historical instances retain their original inline definitions. For example, `9709.p4.pm.apply_constant_acceleration` changes from the P4-01 definition to the new Kinematics wording, leaving the resulting reviewed source with historical instances whose `procedure_model` disagrees with the object referenced by `procedure_model_ref`; the committed source contains 33 such mismatches versus 6 in P4-01. Reuse the existing canonical definition when the ID already exists, or reject conflicting definitions instead of silently overwriting the ontology entry.
